"""Calibrate and evaluate the capture overlap verdict against the real volcanic photographs.

Retained as evidence (``calibration.py.txt``, output ``calibration.log.txt``). Run from the
worktree root with the worktree's own interpreter:

    cp tests/fixtures/capture-overlap/calibration.py.txt /tmp/calibration.py
    uv run python /tmp/calibration.py > tests/fixtures/capture-overlap/calibration.log.txt

Reads only the photographs through the .exulanica symlink and the two fixtures beside this file.
Runs no reconstruction, touches no database, starts no process. The held-out bowl is NOT read.
"""

import dataclasses
import json
import math
import resource
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

import exulanica
from exulanica.capture import Photograph, measure_overlap
from exulanica.capture.verdict import POLICY_V1, verdict_for_measurement

ROOT = Path.cwd()
assert "recovery-readiness" in exulanica.__file__, exulanica.__file__
FIXTURES = ROOT / "tests/fixtures/capture-overlap"
PHOTOS = ROOT / ".exulanica/reference-baseline/inputs/volcanic-sample/photographs"
cameras = json.loads((FIXTURES / "volcanic-cameras.json").read_text())["photographs"]
runs = {run["label"]: run for run in json.loads((FIXTURES / "measured-runs.json").read_text())["runs"]}
names = [camera["name"] for camera in cameras]
assert names == sorted(path.name for path in PHOTOS.iterdir() if path.suffix.lower() == ".jpg")
forward = [[value / 1_000_000 for value in camera["forward_e6"]] for camera in cameras]


def angle(i, j):
    a, b = forward[i], forward[j]
    dot = sum(p * q for p, q in zip(a, b)) / math.sqrt(sum(p * p for p in a) * sum(q * q for q in b))
    return math.degrees(math.acos(max(-1.0, min(1.0, dot))))


def say(*parts):
    print(*parts, flush=True)


say("module", exulanica.__file__)
say("policy", POLICY_V1.version, "edge_min_score", POLICY_V1.edge_min_score)

# 1. The whole 210-photograph verdict, timed end to end, which is the cost a person would wait.
photographs = [Photograph.from_path(name, PHOTOS / name) for name in names]
started = time.perf_counter()
started_cpu = time.process_time()
verdict = verdict_for_measurement(measure_overlap(photographs, POLICY_V1.descriptor))
wall = time.perf_counter() - started
cpu = time.process_time() - started_cpu
peak = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss
say(f"210 verdict: wall {wall:.2f} s, cpu {cpu:.2f} s, peak rss {peak // (1024 * 1024)} MiB (ru_maxrss bytes on darwin)")
say("210 verdict:", verdict.predicted_ceiling, "worth", verdict.worth_attempting,
    "edges", len(verdict.graph.edges), "largest", verdict.graph.largest_component,
    "groups", verdict.graph.groups, "isolated", verdict.graph.isolated,
    "structure", verdict.graph.structure, "digest", verdict.sha256().hex())
measurement = verdict.graph.measurement
ref_index = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(names)}
assert [item.ref for item in measurement.photographs] == names
assert all(item.state == "measured" for item in measurement.photographs)
score = {}
cursor = 0
for a in range(210):
    for b in range(a + 1, 210):
        score[(a, b)] = measurement.pair_scores[cursor]
        cursor += 1

# 2. The threshold rule, on the calibration series, and the same curve on the validation series.
say("\nthreshold rule: J = TPR(pairs <= 21 deg) - FPR(pairs >= 90 deg), per ten thousand")
for label, low, high in (("calibration 0-112", 0, 113), ("validation 113-209", 113, 210)):
    pairs = [(a, b) for (a, b) in score if low <= a and b < high]
    positive = [p for p in pairs if angle(*p) <= 21]
    negative = [p for p in pairs if angle(*p) >= 90]
    line = []
    best = None
    for t in range(3, 17):
        tpr = sum(score[p] >= t for p in positive) * 10000 // len(positive)
        fpr = sum(score[p] >= t for p in negative) * 10000 // len(negative)
        line.append(f"t{t}:{tpr - fpr}(tpr {tpr} fpr {fpr})")
        if best is None or tpr - fpr > best[1]:
            best = (t, tpr - fpr)
    say(f"  {label}: {len(pairs)} pairs, {len(positive)} positive, {len(negative)} negative; maximum J at t={best[0]} ({best[1]})")
    for chunk in range(0, len(line), 4):
        say("    " + "  ".join(line[chunk:chunk + 4]))
    buckets = {}
    for p in pairs:
        buckets.setdefault(min(int(angle(*p) // 10) * 10, 90), []).append(score[p] >= POLICY_V1.edge_min_score)
    say("    edge rate at the policy threshold by 10-degree band: " + " ".join(f"{b}:{100 * sum(v) // len(v)}%" for b, v in sorted(buckets.items())))


def verdict_at(indices, threshold=None):
    policy = POLICY_V1 if threshold is None else dataclasses.replace(POLICY_V1, edge_min_score=threshold)
    return verdict_for_measurement(measurement.subset(names[i] for i in indices), policy)


def neighbour_angles(indices):
    return [round(angle(indices[k], indices[k + 1]), 1) for k in range(len(indices) - 1)]


# 3. The four measured rows, with the verdict at every threshold so the margin is visible.
say("\nthe four measured rows")
outcome_rank = {"insufficient_overlap": 1, "registered_partial": 2, "registered_scene": 3}
for label in ("six", "twelve_wide", "twelve_close", "all_210"):
    run = runs[label]
    indices = run["indices"]
    if run["registered_count"] == 0:
        actual = "insufficient_overlap"
    elif run["accepted"]:
        actual = "registered_scene"
    else:
        actual = "registered_partial"
    v = verdict_at(indices)
    say(f"  {label}: {len(indices)} photographs, receipt {run['receipt_sha256'][:12]} registered {run['registered_count']} of {run['source_count']} accepted {run['accepted']} -> outcome {actual}")
    if len(indices) <= 12:
        say(f"    indices {indices}")
        say(f"    neighbour optical-axis angles (deg) {neighbour_angles(indices)}; first to last {round(angle(indices[0], indices[-1]), 1)}")
        nb = [score[(indices[k], indices[k + 1])] for k in range(len(indices) - 1)]
        others = sorted((score[(min(a, b), max(a, b))] for a in indices for b in indices if a < b and abs(indices.index(a) - indices.index(b)) > 1), reverse=True)
        say(f"    neighbour pair scores {nb}; strongest non-neighbour scores {others[:5]}")
    say(f"    policy verdict: ceiling {v.predicted_ceiling}, worth {v.worth_attempting}, fault {v.fault}, advisories {list(v.advisories)}, largest {v.graph.largest_component}/{v.graph.photograph_count}, groups {v.graph.groups}, isolated {v.graph.isolated}, structure {v.graph.structure}")
    say(f"    consistent with outcome (outcome at or below ceiling, and refusal iff outcome below registered_scene): {outcome_rank[actual] <= outcome_rank[v.predicted_ceiling] and (v.worth_attempting == (actual == 'registered_scene'))}")
    flips = []
    previous = None
    for t in range(1, 41):
        w = verdict_at(indices, t)
        state = (w.predicted_ceiling, w.worth_attempting)
        if state != previous:
            flips.append(f"t>={t}: {w.predicted_ceiling}")
            previous = state
    say(f"    verdict by threshold: {'; '.join(flips)}")
    for line in v.instructions():
        say(f"    says: {line.headline} {line.detail} {line.action or ''}".rstrip())

# 4. Monotonicity. Hold the start and the count fixed, widen the step, and count the sequences in
# which a refusal turns back into a run. Also the run rate by each set's true spacing: the
# smallest angle that links 80 percent of the set, which is what the pose gate's floor needs.
def floor_spacing(indices):
    need = -(-4 * len(indices) // 5)
    parent = {i: i for i in indices}
    size = {i: 1 for i in indices}

    def root(i):
        while parent[i] != i:
            parent[i] = parent[parent[i]]
            i = parent[i]
        return i

    for a, b, t in sorted(((a, b, angle(a, b)) for a in indices for b in indices if a < b), key=lambda x: x[2]):
        ra, rb = root(a), root(b)
        if ra != rb:
            parent[rb] = ra
            size[ra] += size[rb]
            if size[ra] >= need:
                return t
    return 0.0


subsets = {}


def subset(indices):
    if indices not in subsets:
        subsets[indices] = measurement.subset(names[i] for i in indices)
    return subsets[indices]


say("\nmonotonicity sweep: counts 6, 8, 12 and 16, every start, every step that fits")
for threshold in (6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 12):
    policy = dataclasses.replace(POLICY_V1, edge_min_score=threshold)
    line = []
    for label, low, high in (("calibration 0-112", 0, 112), ("validation 113-209", 113, 209)):
        flips = sequences = 0
        bins = {}
        for count in (6, 8, 12, 16):
            for start in range(low, high + 1):
                sequences += 1
                previous, step = None, 1
                while start + step * (count - 1) <= high:
                    indices = tuple(start + step * k for k in range(count))
                    run = verdict_for_measurement(subset(indices), policy).worth_attempting
                    flips += previous is False and run
                    if threshold == POLICY_V1.edge_min_score:
                        bins.setdefault(min(int(floor_spacing(indices) // 5) * 5, 60), []).append(run)
                    previous, step = run, step + 1
        line.append(f"{label}: {flips} of {sequences} sequences turn a refusal back into a run")
        if bins:
            say(f"  run rate at t={threshold} by true 80% spacing, {label}: " + " ".join(f"{b}-{b + 5}deg:{100 * sum(v) // len(v)}%(n{len(v)})" for b, v in sorted(bins.items())))
    say(f"  t={threshold}: " + "; ".join(line))

# 5. Whether a chain closes, read from the thresholded graph two ways, against turntable arcs
# whose extent is known. Neither reading ships: both are recorded here because the package
# docstring cites the better one.
def adjacency_of(graph):
    component = graph.components[0]
    members = set(component)
    adjacency = {n: [] for n in component}
    for a, b in graph.edges:
        if a in members:
            adjacency[a].append(b)
            adjacency[b].append(a)
    return component, adjacency


def bfs(adjacency, start, removed=frozenset()):
    seen = {start: 0}
    frontier = [start]
    while frontier:
        following = []
        for node in frontier:
            for other in sorted(adjacency[node]):
                if other not in seen and other not in removed:
                    seen[other] = seen[node] + 1
                    following.append(other)
        frontier = following
    return seen


def closure_by_layer_spread(graph):
    component, adjacency = adjacency_of(graph)
    distances = {n: bfs(adjacency, n) for n in component}
    diameter = max(max(row.values()) for row in distances.values())
    if diameter < 4:
        return "undetermined"
    end = min(component, key=lambda n: (-max(distances[n].values()), n))
    layer = [n for n in component if distances[end][n] == max(distances[end].values()) // 2]
    spread = max(distances[a][b] for a in layer for b in layer)
    return "closed" if spread >= max(3, diameter // 2) else "open"


def closure_by_removing_a_middle(graph):
    component, adjacency = adjacency_of(graph)
    distances = {n: bfs(adjacency, n) for n in component}
    diameter = max(max(row.values()) for row in distances.values())
    if diameter < 4:
        return "undetermined"
    u = min(component, key=lambda n: (-max(distances[n].values()), n))
    v = min(n for n in component if distances[u][n] == diameter)
    middle = min(n for n in component if distances[u][n] == diameter // 2 and distances[v][n] == diameter - diameter // 2)
    removed = frozenset([middle, *adjacency[middle]])
    return "closed" if v in bfs(adjacency, u, removed) else "open"


say("\nclosure readings against known arcs (ring one is frames 0-35, ring two 36-71)")
cases = []
for step in (1, 2, 3):
    for arc in (90, 150, 180, 240, 270, 330, 360):
        frames = arc // 10
        cases.append((f"ring one step {step} arc {arc}", list(range(0, frames, step)) if arc == 360 else list(range(0, frames + 1, step)), "closed" if arc == 360 else "open"))
for step in (1, 2):
    for arc in (120, 240, 360):
        frames = arc // 10
        cases.append((f"ring two step {step} arc {arc}", [36 + k for k in (range(0, frames, step) if arc == 360 else range(0, frames + 1, step))], "closed" if arc == 360 else "open"))
cases.append(("rings one and two, half a turn each", list(range(0, 19)) + list(range(36, 55)), "open"))
cases.append(("rings one and two, whole", list(range(0, 72)), "closed"))
from exulanica.capture.overlap import overlap_graph
for reader in (closure_by_layer_spread, closure_by_removing_a_middle):
    wrong = determined = 0
    for label, indices, truth in cases:
        graph = overlap_graph(subset(tuple(indices)), POLICY_V1.edge_min_score)
        reading = reader(graph) if graph.largest_component > 1 else "undetermined"
        if reading != "undetermined":
            determined += 1
            wrong += reading != truth
        say(f"  {reader.__name__}: {label}: {reading} (truth {truth})")
    say(f"  {reader.__name__}: {wrong} wrong of {determined} determined, {len(cases) - determined} undetermined")
